name: Button
description: An accessible button that builds on the project's own: variants mapped to its design, sizes that grow with their labels, icon-only names, toggles with aria-pressed, focus rings that survive forced colors, and a busy state that keeps focus and says what's happening.

tokens.note: Suggested defaults. The project's design tokens and existing components win.

aiAgentInstructions.summary: Build or extend a button: a native <button> for actions (links for navigation), variants mapped to the project's design, heights that are minimums, names that include the visible text, icon-only buttons with a name, toggles with aria-pressed, focus rings drawn as outlines, and a busy state that keeps focus and the name (aria-disabled), ignores more presses, and says what's happening in a status region. Build on the project's Button component when it has one. Implement only what the task needs, keep existing APIs, and match the project's styling and tokens. The project's conventions win for styling and visual defaults; if one conflicts with an accessibility or correctness requirement in this guide, ask the user instead of choosing silently. Target WCAG 2.2 AA.
keyFeatures: Native <button> for actions and <a href> for navigation, with type="button" on buttons in a form that don't submit it
A busy state with aria-disabled, not disabled, so focus and the name stay; presses and Enter in the form ignored; progress in a status region; a time limit
Heights as minimums, so labels can wrap; targets of at least 24 px, 44 px suggested on touch screens
Names that include the visible text, and names for icon-only buttons
Focus rings drawn with outline, which forced colors keep
Toggles with aria-pressed and one label
implementationSteps: 1. Detect the framework and its version, the styling system, the tokens, and the existing components (projectDetection). If the project already has a Button component, configure or extend it to meet this guide instead of building another one, and keep its API.
2. Use a button for actions and a link for navigation (implementationDetails.buttonOrLink).
3. Map the variants and sizes the task needs to the project's (componentSpec.variants, implementationDetails.size).
4. Give every button a name and draw the focus ring (implementationDetails.content, implementationDetails.states).
5. Add the busy state where an action takes time (frameworkPatterns.busyButton, implementationDetails.busy), and disabled states and toggles where the task needs them.
6. Check the result against testingChecklist with a keyboard, a screen reader, a phone, forced colors, and 200% text, and run the project's existing tests and checks.

componentSpec.goal: Let people run actions reliably and know what's happening: a button that is easy to find, name, and press, and that keeps focus and says what's happening while its action runs.

anatomy.hierarchy: button (root) → optional leading icon, label, optional trailing icon; while busy, a spinner over the label, which stays in the button

slotNotes.root: A button does something on this page: it saves, opens a dialog, or changes a setting. A link goes somewhere, even when it looks like a button ("Get started" on a landing page). Screen readers say which is which, and links can be opened in a new tab or copied.
slotNotes.label: A button with visible text is named by that text. Extra context goes after it, visually hidden ("Edit", then " profile"), so the name still starts with what people see and can say to voice control (2.5.3); an aria-label that replaces the text breaks that.
slotNotes.icons: Icons are decorative (aria-hidden="true"): 16 to 20 px, 8 px from the text.
slotNotes.spinner: The label stays the button's name. A spinner can sit over the content, which turns transparent (opacity: 0), or beside it in space kept free, so the width doesn't change. visibility: hidden on the label would also remove the name (checked in Chromium's accessibility tree).

variant.description: The visual emphasis, mapped to the project's variants.

size.description: Minimum heights: small 36 px, medium 44 px, large 52 px (suggested).

busy.description: Whether its action runs: aria-disabled, presses ignored, a spinner over the label, and a message in the status region.

unavailable.description: none: usable. disabled: out of the Tab order. aria-disabled: reachable, so people can learn why, with the reason next to it.

pressed.description: For a toggle only: aria-pressed, with one label.

interactions.when: a click, Enter, or Space, and the button isn't busy or aria-disabled
interactions.accessibilityNotes: Native buttons need no key handling.

interactions.when: the button is busy or aria-disabled
interactions.accessibilityNotes: For a submit button, the form's submit handler ignores it, since Enter in a field submits too.
Focus stays on the button, and its name stays.

interactions.when: success, failure, or the time limit

responsiveBehavior.touchScreens: Targets 44 px suggested, icon-only buttons square. A form's primary button can fill the width of a one-column form on phones.
responsiveBehavior.allScreens: Labels wrap and the button grows; nothing scrolls sideways at 320 px wide.

variants.primary: The main action of a view; one per form or dialog.
variants.secondary: Other actions, with a border or a light fill.
variants.ghost: Low emphasis, in dense toolbars, with a clear hover and focus.
variants.destructive: A label that names the action; asks first or can be undone.
variants.link: Looks like a link and stays a button; underlined in running text.
variants.iconOnly: An icon-only button gets its name from aria-label or visually hidden text ("Close", "Edit profile"), and a tooltip can show the same words. It's square: at least 24 px, 44 px suggested on touch screens.
variants.toggle: A toggle button has aria-pressed and one label ("Bold", pressed or not), with the pressed state shown by more than color. A button whose label changes instead ("Mute", then "Unmute") has no aria-pressed: both together read as a double state.

dataContract.props: variant, size, type (button, submit, reset), busy, disabled or aria-disabled with a reason, pressed (toggles), the label, optional icons, and an accessible name for icon-only buttons; with href, it renders a link
dataContract.events: press (not while busy or aria-disabled); for toggles, the new pressed state

press.properties: scale to 0.98 when motion is allowed

animations.reducedMotion: Hover and focus changes take about 120 ms and a press about 80 ms. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, nothing scales or moves, and a spinner turns slower; the status message carries the meaning.

requirements.1.3.1: Native buttons and links, so the role says what each does.
requirements.1.4.1: Link-style buttons in running text are underlined; destructive ones are named by their label, not only their color.
requirements.1.4.4: Labels grow with text size; heights are minimums.
requirements.1.4.11: Focus rings and the borders that mark buttons meet 3:1.
requirements.1.4.12: With text spacing overrides, labels wrap instead of overflowing.
requirements.2.1.1: Native buttons work with Enter and Space.
requirements.2.4.7: The focus ring shows on :focus-visible, and in forced colors.
requirements.2.5.8: Targets are at least 24 by 24 px, or have that much room.
requirements.4.1.2: Names, aria-pressed for toggles, and aria-disabled or disabled.
requirements.4.1.3: Busy and done are said in a status region.

keyboardNavigation.buttons: Tab reaches them; Enter and Space press them, natively.
keyboardNavigation.links: Enter follows them; Space scrolls the page.
keyboardNavigation.busy: Presses while it's busy are ignored in code. For a submit button, the guard goes in the form's submit handler: Enter in a field submits the form even when its button has aria-disabled, in all three engines (checked).

button.type: "button" for a button in a form that doesn't submit it

iconOnly.aria-label: The action, such as "Close", unless visually hidden text names it

unavailable.aria-disabled: "true", with the reason linked by aria-describedby
unavailable.disabled: when people don't need to reach it

screenReader.busy: aria-busy on a button isn't announced reliably. A status region that's in the page from the start says what's happening ("Saving…") and how it ended ("Saved", or what went wrong), as in the Login & Registration and Form Validation guides.
screenReader.toggle: A toggle button has aria-pressed and one label ("Bold", pressed or not), with the pressed state shown by more than color. A button whose label changes instead ("Mute", then "Unmute") has no aria-pressed: both together read as a double state.

focusManagement.busy: While its action runs, a button stays focusable and keeps its name: aria-disabled="true", not disabled. Setting disabled on the focused button drops focus to the top of the page in Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit (checked), so keyboard and screen reader users lose their place.
focusManagement.focusRing: Focus shows on :focus-visible with an outline 2 px wide and 2 px out, at 3:1 against the background. Draw it with outline: forced colors (Windows' contrast themes) drop box shadows, while an outline stays, even a transparent one (checked in Chromium). A ring drawn as a shadow keeps a transparent outline under it.

framework.description: Find the framework, its version, and how existing components are written before writing code.
detectionSteps: Read the project's dependencies (package.json or its equivalent) for the framework and its version, and use the syntax that version supports.
Open two or three existing components to see their file structure, state handling, and naming.
Look for an existing component that already does this job, in the project or in a design system or UI library it uses, and build on it.

stylingSystem.description: Use the styling system the project already uses, and only that one.
detectionSteps: Check the dependencies and config for the styling setup: Tailwind (version 4 keeps its theme in CSS with @theme, version 3 in tailwind.config.*), CSS Modules, Sass, CSS-in-JS, or plain CSS.
See how existing components apply styles and compose class names, for example with cn or clsx.
Check for design documentation: DESIGN.md, a design system package, or Storybook stories for existing components.
adaptationRules: Write styles the way existing components do, and add no new styling library or system.
With plain CSS, use classes in the project's stylesheets instead of inline styles, except for values computed at runtime.
If the setup is unclear or mixed, ask before choosing.

designTokens.description: Use the project's tokens for color, spacing, radius, type, shadows, motion, and layering.
detectionSteps: Find the tokens: CSS custom properties, a Tailwind theme (@theme or config), a theme object, or a tokens file.
Use them instead of this guide's example values; where there are none, match the closest existing components.
Check that the colors you use meet the contrast minimums: 4.5:1 for text, and 3:1 for focus indicators, icons, and control boundaries.

frameworkPatterns.note: Short snippets in plain HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for the parts that are easiest to get wrong; adapt them to the project's framework and its version.

busyButton.description: A submit button with a busy state: aria-disabled, so it keeps focus and its name; a second submit ignored in the form's submit handler, Enter in a field included; "Saving…" and the outcome in a status region that's in the page from the start; a time limit; a spinner over the content, which turns transparent rather than hidden, so the width and the name stay and an icon keeps its place beside the label; min-height; an outline focus ring; and a slower spinner under reduced motion. save() stands for the app's request.

implementationDetails.buttonOrLink: A button does something on this page: it saves, opens a dialog, or changes a setting. A link goes somewhere, even when it looks like a button ("Get started" on a landing page). Screen readers say which is which, and links can be opened in a new tab or copied. A button in a form submits it unless it says otherwise, so every other button in a form has type="button". A link that looks like a button stays an <a href>, and a button that looks like a link stays a <button>. Enter presses both; Space presses a button and scrolls the page on a link, so a link that does a button's job becomes a button, not a link with a Space handler. A link that can't be followed yet is rendered without href: Tab skips it, and screen readers read it as text (checked: Tab skips it in Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit).
implementationDetails.variants: Map the variants to the project's own: primary for the main action of a view (one per form or dialog), secondary, ghost for low emphasis in dense toolbars, destructive, and link-style. Leave out the ones the task doesn't need. A destructive button is marked by more than its color: its label names the action ("Delete project"), and the action asks first (the Modal Dialog guide) or can be undone (the Toast Notifications guide). A link-style button in running text is underlined, like the links around it (1.4.1).
implementationDetails.size: The height is a minimum (min-height), never a fixed height: a label that wraps, after translation, at 200% text, or with text spacing overrides, makes the button taller instead of overflowing it (1.4.4, 1.4.12). Checked: with a fixed 36 px height, a two-line label overflows the button in all three engines; with min-height, the button grows. Suggested sizes: small 36 px, medium 44 px, and large 52 px high, with 12 to 16 px of padding on each side. Targets are at least 24 by 24 px, or have that much room around them (2.5.8); 44 px is the suggested size on touch screens.
implementationDetails.content: A button with visible text is named by that text. Extra context goes after it, visually hidden ("Edit", then " profile"), so the name still starts with what people see and can say to voice control (2.5.3); an aria-label that replaces the text breaks that. An icon-only button gets its name from aria-label or visually hidden text ("Close", "Edit profile"), and a tooltip can show the same words. It's square: at least 24 px, 44 px suggested on touch screens. Icons are decorative (aria-hidden="true"): 16 to 20 px, 8 px from the text.
implementationDetails.states: Hover and press feedback, a color change and an optional scale to 0.98, never moves the layout. The pointer cursor is a style choice; follow the project. Focus shows on :focus-visible with an outline 2 px wide and 2 px out, at 3:1 against the background. Draw it with outline: forced colors (Windows' contrast themes) drop box shadows, while an outline stays, even a transparent one (checked in Chromium). A ring drawn as a shadow keeps a transparent outline under it. Prefer a button that stays enabled and says what's missing when it's pressed, as the Form Validation guide does for submit buttons. An action that really can't be used now gets disabled, which takes the button out of the Tab order; or aria-disabled="true" when people need to reach it to learn why, with the reason next to it and linked by aria-describedby. Code ignores presses on an aria-disabled button. Disabled styles don't rely on opacity alone, and pointer-events: none would also hide the "not allowed" cursor. A toggle button has aria-pressed and one label ("Bold", pressed or not), with the pressed state shown by more than color. A button whose label changes instead ("Mute", then "Unmute") has no aria-pressed: both together read as a double state.
implementationDetails.busy: While its action runs, a button stays focusable and keeps its name: aria-disabled="true", not disabled. Setting disabled on the focused button drops focus to the top of the page in Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit (checked), so keyboard and screen reader users lose their place. Presses while it's busy are ignored in code. For a submit button, the guard goes in the form's submit handler: Enter in a field submits the form even when its button has aria-disabled, in all three engines (checked). The label stays the button's name. A spinner can sit over the content, which turns transparent (opacity: 0), or beside it in space kept free, so the width doesn't change. visibility: hidden on the label would also remove the name (checked in Chromium's accessibility tree). aria-busy on a button isn't announced reliably. A status region that's in the page from the start says what's happening ("Saving…") and how it ended ("Saved", or what went wrong), as in the Login & Registration and Form Validation guides. The busy state ends on success, on failure, and at a time limit, such as 30 seconds, so a request that hangs can't leave the button stuck.
implementationDetails.motion: Hover and focus changes take about 120 ms and a press about 80 ms. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, nothing scales or moves, and a spinner turns slower; the status message carries the meaning.
implementationDetails.appearance: Suggested defaults; the project's design and tokens win. A 6 to 8 px radius, a font weight of 600, and the sizes above. Labels meet 4.5:1 against the button, and the focus ring and any border that marks the button's edge 3:1 against what's around it: a primary button in #2563eb with white text is 5.2:1, while #3b82f6 is 3.7:1; a destructive one in #b91c1c is 6.5:1, while #ef4444 is 3.8:1; a secondary button's #767676 border is 4.5:1 on white. Check the project's own colors.

edgeCases.longLabels: A label that grows, after translation for example, wraps or widens the button; it's never cut off.
edgeCases.nesting: A button inside a link, or a link inside a button: interactive elements can't nest, so make them siblings.
edgeCases.quickActions: An action that's over in a moment can skip the spinner, but not aria-disabled and the guard.
edgeCases.doubleClick: A double click on a button that submits: the busy guard ignores the second one.

must: Build on the project's Button component when it has one, and keep its API
Use buttons for actions and links for navigation, with type="button" on buttons in a form that don't submit it
Keep focus and the name while busy, with aria-disabled, and ignore presses and Enter in the form
Give every button a name that includes its visible text
Use the project's framework version, styling system, and tokens, the way existing components do
mustNot: Set disabled on a button while its action runs
Give buttons a fixed height, or hide a busy label with visibility: hidden
Draw the focus ring only with box-shadow, or remove it
Use a div or span with role="button", or a link that does a button's job
Use inline styles for static values in a plain-CSS project, or hardcode colors the project has tokens for

testingChecklist: Actions are buttons and navigation is links; a button in a form that doesn't submit it has type="button"
Every button has a name that includes its visible text; an icon-only button gets one from aria-label or visually hidden text, and its icon is hidden from screen readers
Buttons are at least 24 by 24 px (44 px suggested on touch screens), and their height is a minimum, so a label that wraps makes them taller
The focus ring shows with the keyboard, meets 3:1, and is an outline, so it stays in forced colors
While busy, a button has aria-disabled="true", keeps focus and its name, and ignores presses; a form also ignores Enter in its fields
A busy state is said in a status region that's in the page from the start, and ends on success, on failure, and at a time limit
A busy button keeps its width, and its spinner turns slower under reduced motion
A button that can't be used now has disabled, or aria-disabled when people need to reach it and learn why, which is said next to it
A toggle keeps one label and changes aria-pressed, or changes its label without aria-pressed, never both
Link-styled buttons and links in running text are underlined
A destructive action's label names it, and the action asks first or can be undone
Labels meet 4.5:1, and the focus ring and any border that marks the button 3:1
Hover and press feedback never move the layout, and under reduced motion nothing scales
Styles come from the project's styling system and tokens
